ety.text: Borrowed from French cuisine (“cooking, culinary art, kitchen”), from Late Latin cocīna, from earlier coquīna (“kitchen”). Doublet of kitchen.

senses.d: A characteristic manner or style of preparing food, often associated with a place of origin.
ex: French cuisine is considered to be one of the world's most refined and elegant styles of cooking.
The restaurant is noted for its excellent cuisine.

senses.d: The food prepared using such style.
Synonym of culinary art: The art of preparing food in general.

ety.text: Inherited from Old French cuisine (“kitchen; cooking, cooked food”), from Late Latin cocīna, from earlier coquīna (“kitchen”). First attested in the 12th century. Cognate with English kitchen.
From Late Latin cocīna, from earlier coquīna.

Proto-Indo-European *gres-der. Ancient Greek γρᾰ́ω (grắō) Proto-Indo-European *-tḗr Proto-Hellenic *-tḗr Ancient Greek -τήρ (-tḗr) Ancient Greek γᾰστήρ (găstḗr)der. Spanish gastro- Spanish -nomia Spanish gastronomía From gastro- + -nomia.
Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese cozinha, from Late Latin cocīna, from earlier coquīna. Compare Galician cociña, Asturian and Spanish cocina, French cuisine.
